# TextStats project brief

## Purpose and audience

TextStats is a small Python utility for developers and command-line users who need predictable line and word counts for UTF-8 text. It will expose a silent importable API and a module-entry CLI with explicit output and failure contracts. This repository currently contains preparation documents only; functionality has not been implemented.

## Established requirements

The product request establishes Python 3.11+, the standard library and unittest. The public `textstats` module must directly export immutable `TextStats(lines: int, words: int)` with nonnegative values, `count_text(text: str, *, strip_bom: bool = True)` and `count_file(path: str | os.PathLike[str], *, strip_bom: bool = True)`. The CLI entry is `python -m textstats`.

Line counting recognizes CRLF as one terminator and lone CR or LF as terminators. Each terminator contributes one line; a nonempty final unterminated segment contributes one. Empty input has zero lines, trailing terminators create no phantom line, and other Unicode separators do not terminate lines. Words follow Python `str.split` Unicode whitespace semantics.

By default, remove exactly one leading U+FEFF. Preserve interior BOMs and every BOM when `strip_bom=False` or `--keep-bom` is selected. A retained BOM is ordinary non-whitespace. Files decode as strict UTF-8; API failures retain OSError subclasses or UnicodeDecodeError, produce no partial result, and close owned handles. API calls are silent and inputs remain unchanged.

## Delivery boundaries

| Phase and milestone | Intended useful outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Phase 1, milestone 1.1 | Named-file counting through the public API and `python -m textstats [--keep-bom] INPUT`; exactly one input and `--` for dash-prefixed filenames. Success returns 0 with exactly `lines=<N> words=<N>\n` on stdout and empty stderr; help returns 0. |
| Phase 1, milestone 1.2 | Failure handling, public API/module documentation, runnable README and distribution exits. Input/read/decode failures return 1; missing/extra inputs and unknown options return 2. Failures identify the problem on stderr with empty stdout and no traceback. |
| Phase 2, milestone 2.1 | Historical JSON increment withdrawn. Current output is exact text; `--json` is an unknown-option usage error before acquisition. A literal `--json` filename works after `--`. |
| Phase 2, milestone 2.2 | `-` reads stdin bytes to EOF and decodes UTF-8 independently of locale without closing stdin. Empty stdin counts (0, 0); read/decode errors return 1 and identify stdin. Final exits cover documentation, distribution and retained behavior. |

Product tests must be discoverable and nonempty under `tests/unit/` and `tests/integration/`. Workflow fixture checks belong separately under `tests/workflows/`. Distribution verification must invoke the extracted source package's module entry. Exact test commands and package layout will be established during planning, rather than claimed as runnable at this stage.

## Later separately requested range feature

Retain this feature as a future design constraint and separate delivery boundary, outside the initial two-phase executable hierarchy. It will add exactly one `--lines START:END` or `--lines=START:END`, using positive ASCII decimal inclusive one-based endpoints with START <= END and decimal leading zeros. There is no arbitrary endpoint limit. Reject signs, whitespace, Unicode digits, zero, reversed endpoints, open endpoints, extra colons, missing values and repeated range options with usage status 2 before acquiring input.

Complete input must decode before selection, including bytes after END. Apply BOM policy once before line numbering, preserve selected content and terminators, and select the available subset or zero beyond EOF. Exposing an interior BOM must not strip it. Options compose in either order. Public API signatures and exports stay whole-input. Named-file text range behavior is this feature's delivery boundary; source-independent compatibility with future stdin is required, while stdin acquisition and delivery remain their own later milestone.

## Acceptance anchors

The eventual specification must retain the full supplied examples and invalid-range matrix. Key anchors are empty input (0, 0), BOM-only default (0, 0), retained BOM (1, 1), two leading BOMs under default policy (1, 1), LF-only (1, 0), `alpha\n\n` (2, 1), and `alpha` followed by U+2028 and `beta` (1, 2). These distinguish terminator counting, Unicode word splitting and exactly-once BOM removal.

For `alpha beta\nbeta\nlast two`, ranges 2:3 and 2:99 yield (2, 3), 1:1 yields (1, 2), and 4:99 yields (0, 0). Blank selected lines and mixed CRLF/CR/LF must retain their counts. No new performance targets, third-party runtime dependencies or extra CLI capabilities are inferred.

## Preparation scope and review

The authorized workflow prepares PROJECT, architecture, decomposition, specification, plan, layout and an executable task hierarchy, pausing for each necessary new document's human review. Stop before production implementation; phase 2 and the later feature are not being implemented by this request.

The supplied product request establishes the requirements; this document organizes them and does not assert acceptance of unseen downstream documents. No consequential product decision is currently unresolved.

# TextStats architecture

## Scope and governing input

This document describes the intended architecture for the capabilities and staged scope in the accepted [project brief](PROJECT.md). No product implementation exists. The public surface is an importable `textstats` API and `python -m textstats`; counting has no runtime dependencies beyond Python 3.11+ and the standard library.

## Major blocks and dependency direction

| Block | Responsibility and dependencies |
| --- | --- |
| Counting core | Own immutable statistics and text semantics: BOM normalization, CRLF/CR/LF logical-line handling and Unicode whitespace word counting. It depends on Python strings and immutable results, with no filesystem, CLI or process-stream dependency. |
| Input acquisition | Own strict UTF-8 decoding and named-file handle lifetime. It supplies decoded text to the counting pipeline and propagates acquisition/decode errors. Future stdin acquisition uses bytes and retains external stream ownership. |
| Public API facade | Directly expose the three requested public exports. `count_text` invokes the text pipeline; `count_file` acquires named-file text and invokes equivalent whole-input counting. Both return statistics silently, retaining API exceptions. |
| CLI orchestration | Parse and validate the requested invocation before acquiring input, select BOM policy, invoke the counting pipeline and translate input failures into CLI diagnostics/status. It depends on acquisition and core contracts; neither depends on CLI. |
| Presentation | Format a completed result as the required text output. The CLI owns stdout/stderr effects and process status; presentation contains no input acquisition or counting rules. |

These are logical responsibility blocks, not a requirement for separate files or classes. Detailed collaborating components belong in decomposition and physical allocation in layout. There is no dependency cycle or global mutable counting state. The API and CLI share counting and decoding semantics rather than maintaining independent algorithms.

## Text pipeline and ownership

Acquisition finishes strict decoding before a result can be computed or emitted. The text pipeline removes at most one leading BOM according to the selected policy, then operates on normalized text. Whole-input API calls never select a range. The pipeline provides a counting path for already normalized text so the later CLI range path cannot strip a newly exposed interior BOM.

A shared logical-line representation or traversal recognizes only CRLF, CR and LF and preserves terminators and content. Both counting and future selection must use this semantic boundary; Python's broader Unicode `splitlines` behavior is unsuitable. Word counting remains independent, using `str.split` semantics on the counted content. Decomposition will settle the small internal interfaces without adding public exports.

The future range pipeline is acquisition and complete decode, BOM normalization once, logical-line selection, then counting and presentation. Parsing/validation precedes acquisition. Selection does not depend on whether text originated from a file or stdin. This supports the requested compatibility constraint without implementing the range feature or moving stdin into its delivery scope.

Input acquisition owns handles it opens and closes them on success and failure. Callers retain ownership of supplied process streams, including future stdin. No block writes input content. Statistics are immutable values; transient decoded strings and selected content have invocation-local lifetime. The default architecture holds complete decoded input in memory, which simplifies strict complete-decode and no-partial-result guarantees. No bounded-memory target was requested; streaming remains a future reconsideration if a concrete input-size constraint arises.

## Failure and output boundaries

API adapters allow the required filesystem and decode exception types to reach callers and produce no output. CLI orchestration distinguishes usage failures from input/read/decode failures and maps them to the prescribed statuses. Successful acquisition and counting must complete before stdout emission; diagnostics identify the affected input, and expected user failures do not expose a traceback. Presentation receives a complete immutable result, preventing partial count output during read/decode failure.

The CLI emits only the exact text output. Removed JSON options fail during parsing before acquisition. Byte acquisition for future stdin keeps strict UTF-8 decoding independent of locale. Option parsing is a CLI concern and does not alter public whole-input API signatures.

## Consequential choices and verification seams

Use plain functions and a small immutable result value. Separate pure text processing from I/O and process effects because they have different failure/lifetime rules and verification seams. A monolithic CLI would couple reusable API behavior to streams; a class hierarchy, plugin system or configurable decoding layer would introduce unsupported variation. The selected function pipeline provides the required extension seams with less state and indirection.

Unit tests can exercise immutable results, BOM policy and logical-line/word semantics directly. Integration tests can exercise named-file acquisition, subprocess CLI output/status, later stdin behavior and extracted-source module execution. Product suites remain nonempty and discoverable under the requested unit/integration directories; coordinator workflow fixtures stay separately owned. API/module documentation and README usage will expose the same contracts used by these checks.

The distribution boundary is a source package that remains importable and supports module execution after extraction. Package contents and the executable verification command are planning/layout decisions. No additional runtime dependency, installed console-script entry or network service is required.

## Review and next stage

Owner review checked responsibility ownership, acyclic dependency direction, strict UTF-8 and handle lifetime, no-partial-result boundaries, BOM normalization exactly once, shared terminator semantics and source-independent future selection against the accepted PROJECT. No unresolved architectural decision blocks decomposition. No focused children are needed for this compact system, and no code or performance test has been run for the proposed arrangement.

| --- | --- | --- |
| C-001 Statistics value | Public immutable `TextStats(lines: int, words: int)` with nonnegative counts. Own construction invariants and value representation. | No acquisition, output or normalization. SPEC will settle invalid-construction exceptions and integer-domain details. |
| C-002 BOM normalization | Internal `normalize_text(text, strip_bom) -> str`; remove exactly one leading BOM when selected and retain all other characters. Own this policy once per pipeline invocation. | Strings only; no decode, line selection or counting. |
| C-003 Logical-line traversal | Internal `logical_lines(normalized_text)` yields nonempty logical segments with their original content and CRLF/CR/LF terminators; blank terminated lines remain segments. A final nonempty unterminated segment is yielded; empty text yields none. | No BOM handling or Unicode-whitespace splitting. This is the shared line boundary for counting and future selection. |
| C-004 Normalized counting | Internal `count_normalized(normalized_text) -> TextStats`; derive line count from C-003 and word count from `str.split` on the same text. | C-001 and C-003; never normalize again, acquire input or emit output. |
| C-005 Byte acquisition and decode | Acquire complete bytes from a named file and decode strict UTF-8 without text newline translation. Own opening and closing named-file handles on every path. Future borrowed-stdin acquisition reads its binary stream to EOF and never closes it. | Python filesystem/binary stream operations; no BOM removal, range selection, counting or output. Preserve acquisition and decode exceptions for callers. |
| C-006 Public API adapters | Directly expose C-001 plus `count_text(text: str, *, strip_bom: bool = True)` and `count_file(path: str | os.PathLike[str], *, strip_bom: bool = True)`. Adapt whole-input requests to C-002/C-004; file calls use C-005 first. | No CLI invocation or range argument; no extra public export, stream output or exception-to-status translation. |
| C-007 CLI invocation parser | Validate option syntax and exactly one input; provide input identity and BOM policy. Future range validation supplies numeric endpoints before input acquisition. | No C-005 access during parsing. Help and usage termination belong to CLI control, not API behavior. |
| C-008 CLI controller | Coordinate parsed invocation, acquisition, text pipeline and result rendering; map expected usage/acquisition/decode failures to identifying diagnostics/status. Own process-stream writes. | C-007, C-005, C-002, C-004 and C-009; no separate counting algorithm. Future C-010 sits between normalization and counting. |
| C-009 Result rendering | Internal renderer transforms completed C-001 into the specified text string plus newline. | No stream write, acquisition, normalization or counting. Controller emits the result. |
| C-010 Future range selection | Future internal `select_lines(normalized_text, start, end) -> str`, with inclusive one-based endpoints, preserving available selected segments and their terminators. | C-003 and validated CLI endpoints; no input-source dependency or BOM normalization. This future feature is outside the initial two-phase executable hierarchy. |

The identities group coherent verification obligations and provide downstream specification/planning traceability; they do not require one module or task per row. No focused children are necessary for this compact component set.

## Collaboration and data lifetime

`count_text` receives the complete string, normalizes through C-002 and counts through C-004. `count_file` uses C-005 to acquire/decode complete input, then follows the equivalent public whole-input pipeline. The API adapters return C-001 without writing stdout/stderr. Strict byte decoding preserves CRLF, lone CR and LF exactly rather than relying on universal-newline text mode.

The CLI parses and validates before C-005 acquires input. C-008 then normalizes exactly once and passes normalized text to C-004. Only a completed value reaches C-009 and only the controller writes its output. If the future range feature is separately requested, C-008 passes normalized text through C-010 first and sends its result directly to C-004, bypassing C-002 a second time. Consequently, a BOM exposed inside selected content remains ordinary non-whitespace.

C-003 yields segments such as `a\r\n`, `b c\r` and `d\n` without changing characters. Selecting whole segments and concatenating them preserves line boundaries for C-004 and preserves Unicode whitespace for word counting. Segment enumeration can be lazy over the already decoded string; it does not imply streaming decode or partial input acceptance. Counting and range selection share the same terminator semantics.

For future stdin, C-005 obtains bytes from the externally owned binary input stream and returns decoded text after EOF; the remainder of the pipeline is identical. The parser/controller activate that acquisition choice only at its delivery milestone. Decoded strings, segments and results are local to an invocation; there is no shared mutable counting state or input mutation.

## Failure and verification seams

C-001 can be checked through construction, immutability and value assertions. C-002 can be checked with empty, BOM-only, repeated-leading and interior-BOM strings under both policies. C-003/C-004 can be checked with mixed terminators, consecutive blank lines, final segments and Unicode whitespace/separators. These seams need no filesystem or subprocess.

C-005 can be checked with temporary valid/invalid UTF-8 files, missing/unreadable paths and controlled read failures, including handle cleanup. Borrowed-stream checks later verify byte decoding, locale independence, EOF and retained ownership. C-006 checks establish direct imports, whole-input equivalence, silence and exception propagation. No partial decoded/count result is returned on input failure.

C-007 checks establish help/usage behavior and, later, range validation before acquisition, including repeated options and unbounded decimal endpoints. C-008/C-009 checks establish exact text output, removed-option rejection, empty failure stdout and identifying stderr/status. Subprocess integration validates the real module entry and extracted-source distribution; component-level seams support controlled acquisition failures that can be difficult to reproduce reliably through platform permissions.

C-010's future checks cover available subsets, beyond-EOF emptiness, blank selected lines, mixed terminators, bad bytes after END and interior BOM exposure. These are deferred feature obligations, not tests or delivery included in this preparation request.

## Contract handoff and review

The product request already fixes line/word/BOM semantics, API signatures, output and exit categories. SPEC will provide the full objective acceptance matrix, exact staged CLI grammar, invalid constructor/input-type contracts where required, useful diagnostic expectations and the public documentation/distribution obligations. Internal naming is provisional; public exports are fixed. There is no unresolved component decision that requires upstream architecture revision.

Owner review checked one owner per responsibility, acyclic collaboration, preservation of binary-decoded newlines, once-only normalization, source independence, lifetime/error seams, component cohesion and localized testability against the accepted architecture. No code or product tests were run. import io
import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch

from textstats import TextStats, count_file


class FileAcquisitionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_success_closes_owned_binary_handle_and_preserves_terminators(self):
        stream = io.BytesIO(b"a\r\nb\rc\n")
        with patch("textstats.io.open", return_value=stream, create=True) as opener:
            self.assertEqual(count_file("named"), TextStats(3, 3))
        opener.assert_called_once_with("named", "rb")
        self.assertTrue(stream.closed)

    def test_decode_failure_closes_and_returns_no_partial_count(self):
        stream = io.BytesIO(b"valid\n\xff")
        with patch("textstats.io.open", return_value=stream, create=True):
            with self.assertRaises(UnicodeDecodeError):
                count_file("named")
        self.assertTrue(stream.closed)

    def test_read_failure_preserves_exception_and_closes(self):
        class BrokenReader(io.BytesIO):
            def read(self, *args):
                raise OSError("controlled read failure")
        stream = BrokenReader()
        with patch("textstats.io.open", return_value=stream, create=True):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(OSError, "controlled read failure"):
                count_file("named")
        self.assertTrue(stream.closed)

    def test_open_failure_preserves_oserror_subclasses(self):
        for failure in [PermissionError("unreadable"), FileNotFoundError("missing"), IsADirectoryError("directory")]:
            with self.subTest(failure=type(failure)):
                with patch("textstats.io.open", side_effect=failure, create=True):
                    with self.assertRaises(type(failure)) as raised:
                        count_file("named")
                self.assertIs(raised.exception, failure)

class CliTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_removed_json_forms_reject_before_all_acquisition(self):
        for option in ['--json', '--json=true', '--j']:
            for args in [[option, 'named'], ['named', option],
                         ['--keep-bom', option, 'named'],
                         ['--lines=1:1', 'named', option]]:
                with self.subTest(args=args):
                    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
                    with patch('textstats.io.open', return_value=io.BytesIO(b'a'), create=True) as acquire, patch('textstats.cli.count_file', return_value=TextStats(1, 1)) as counter:
                        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
                            status = main(args)
                    self.assertEqual((status, out.getvalue()), (2, ''))
                    self.assertIn('usage:', err.getvalue())
                    self.assertIn('error:', err.getvalue())
                    self.assertNotIn('Traceback', err.getvalue())
                    acquire.assert_not_called()
                    counter.assert_not_called()

                status = main(['named'])
        self.assertEqual((status, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()), (0, 'lines=3 words=4\n', ''))
        counter.assert_called_once_with('named', strip_bom=True)

        for args in [['--keep-bom', 'named'], ['named', '--keep-bom']]:

                with patch('textstats.cli.count_file', return_value=TextStats(1, 1)) as counter:
                    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):

                counter.assert_called_once_with('named', strip_bom=False)

                self.assertEqual(main(['--', '--keep-bom']), 0)

            counter.assert_not_called()
            self.assertIn('usage:', out.getvalue())
            self.assertIn('--keep-bom', out.getvalue())
            self.assertEqual(err.getvalue(), '')

    def test_expected_input_failures_have_status_and_diagnostic(self):
        failures = [FileNotFoundError('missing input'), PermissionError('access denied'),
                    OSError('controlled read failure'), UnicodeDecodeError('utf-8', b'\xff', 0, 1, 'invalid start byte')]
        for failure in failures:
            with self.subTest(failure=type(failure).__name__):
                out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
                with patch('textstats.cli.count_file', side_effect=failure):

                self.assertEqual(out.getvalue(), '')
                self.assertIn('affected.txt', err.getvalue())

                self.assertNotIn('Traceback', err.getvalue())

    def test_usage_validates_before_acquisition(self):

            with self.subTest(args=args):

                with patch('textstats.cli.count_file') as counter:
                    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
                        status = main(args)
                counter.assert_not_called()
                self.assertEqual((status, out.getvalue()), (2, ''))

                self.assertIn('error:', err.getvalue())
                self.assertNotIn('Traceback', err.getvalue())

class RangeCliTests(unittest.TestCase):
    INVALID = ['0:1', '1:0', '3:2', '-1:2', '+1:2', '1:-2', '1:+2',
               ' 1:2', '1:2 ', '1 :2', '1:\t2', '١:٢', '１:２', ':2', '1:', ':', '1:2:3', '1', '']

    def invoke(self, args):
        out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
            status = main(args)
        return status, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()

    def test_full_invalid_matrix_precedes_file_acquisition(self):
        invalid = [[ '--lines', value, 'missing'] for value in self.INVALID]
        invalid += [['--lines='+value, 'missing'] for value in self.INVALID]
        invalid += [['missing', '--lines'], ['missing', '--lines='],
                    ['--lines', '--json', 'missing'],
                    ['--lines', '1:2', '--lines', '1:2', 'missing'],
                    ['--lines=1:2', '--lines=1:2', 'missing'],
                    ['--lines', '1:2', '--lines=1:2', 'missing']]
        for args in invalid:
            with self.subTest(args=args), patch('textstats.io.open', create=True) as acquire:
                status, out, err = self.invoke(args)
                self.assertEqual((status, out), (2, ''))
                self.assertIn('usage:', err)
                self.assertNotIn('Traceback', err)
                acquire.assert_not_called()

    def test_real_acquisition_normalizes_once_and_closes(self):
        for options in [[], ['--keep-bom']]:
            stream = io.BytesIO('\ufeffa\n\ufeff'.encode())
            with patch('textstats.io.open', return_value=stream, create=True) as acquire:
                status, out, err = self.invoke(['--lines=2:2', 'named', *options])
            self.assertEqual((status, err), (0, ''))
            self.assertEqual(out, 'lines=1 words=1\n')
            acquire.assert_called_once_with('named', 'rb')
            self.assertTrue(stream.closed)

    def test_full_decode_after_end_and_read_failure_close(self):
        class BrokenReader(io.BytesIO):
            def read(self, *args):
                raise OSError('controlled complete read failure')
        for stream, cause in [(io.BytesIO(b'a\n\xff'), 'utf-8'), (BrokenReader(), 'controlled complete read failure')]:
            with patch('textstats.io.open', return_value=stream, create=True):
                status, out, err = self.invoke(['--lines', '1:1', 'named'])
            self.assertEqual((status, out), (1, ''))
            self.assertIn('named', err)
            self.assertIn(cause, err)
            self.assertNotIn('Traceback', err)
            self.assertTrue(stream.closed)

    def test_valid_huge_and_leading_zero_decimals_do_not_use_conversion_guard(self):
        huge = '9' * 5001
        for value, expected in [('1:'+huge, (2, 2)), (huge+':'+huge, (0,0)),
                                ('0'*5001+'1:'+'0'*5001+'1', (1,1))]:
            with patch('textstats.io.open', return_value=io.BytesIO(b'a\nb'), create=True):
                status, out, err = self.invoke(['named', '--lines='+value])
            self.assertEqual((status,out,err),(0,f'lines={expected[0]} words={expected[1]}\n',''))

# TextStats

Count logical lines and Unicode whitespace words in complete text or a named UTF-8 file. TextStats runs from a source checkout with Python 3.11+ and the standard library; installation and third-party dependencies are unnecessary. The silent API and named-file command support BOM policy, clean errors and exact text output. Named-file line ranges are delivered; stdin remains planned.

## Quick start

Run from the repository root:

```bash
python -c "from pathlib import Path; Path('sample.txt').write_bytes(b'alpha beta\r\nbeta\rlast two\n')"
python -m textstats sample.txt
python -m textstats --help
```

The counting command prints `lines=3 words=5` followed by a newline, with status 0 and empty stderr. Help returns 0 and explains the input and options without opening a file. Inputs stay unchanged.

```bash
python -c "from pathlib import Path; Path('bom.txt').write_bytes(b'\xef\xbb\xbf')"
python -m textstats bom.txt
python -m textstats --keep-bom bom.txt
python -c "from pathlib import Path; Path('-sample').write_bytes(b'alpha beta\n')"
python -m textstats -- -sample
```

BOM-only input produces `lines=0 words=0` by default and `lines=1 words=1` with `--keep-bom`. The dash-prefixed file produces `lines=1 words=2`. Options can appear before or after INPUT; `--` ends option parsing. At this phase a literal `-` is a filename. Exactly one file is required.

Missing, unreadable, read-failing or invalid UTF-8 input returns status 1 with identifying input/cause stderr, no traceback and empty stdout. Missing/extra inputs or unknown options return status 2 with useful usage/error stderr and empty stdout. Invocation validation precedes file access. No partial statistics are emitted.

`--json` output is unsupported. Existing JSON callers must use the text output;
`--json`, `--json=value` and abbreviated `--j` are usage errors (status 2)
before input acquisition. A file literally named `--json` works after `--`.

## Named-file ranges

Select inclusive one-based logical lines with one `--lines START:END` or
`--lines=START:END`. Both compose with BOM options before or after INPUT:

```bash
python -m textstats --lines 2:3 sample.txt
python -m textstats sample.txt --lines=0002:0099
```

Both produce two lines and three words. Endpoints are nonempty positive ASCII
decimals with START <= END. Leading zeros are decimal; there is no endpoint-size
cap. An end past EOF selects available lines, and a start past EOF selects empty
content (`lines=0 words=0`). Only CRLF, CR and LF terminate logical lines; blank
terminated lines count, and a trailing terminator adds no phantom line. Unicode
whitespace still determines words independently.

Complete strict UTF-8 decode occurs before once-only whole-input BOM policy,
line numbering and selection. Selected characters and terminators are preserved;
an interior BOM exposed by selection is retained. Bad bytes after END still fail
with status 1 and no counts. Input bytes remain unchanged. These examples use
both BOM policies:

```bash
python -c "from pathlib import Path; Path('range.txt').write_bytes(b'\xef\xbb\xbfalpha beta\r\n\r\n\xef\xbb\xbf\nlast two')"
python -m textstats --lines 2:2 range.txt
python -m textstats range.txt --keep-bom --lines=2:2
python -m textstats --lines 2:99 range.txt
python -m textstats --keep-bom --lines 3:3 range.txt
python -m textstats range.txt --lines 99:100
```

The outputs have counts 1/0, 1/0, 3/3, 1/1 and 0/0, respectively. The selected
third line retains its interior BOM as a word. All commands return 0 with empty
stderr, with the same exact text format as whole-input output.

Malformed, missing or repeated ranges return status 2 before file access, with
empty stdout and useful usage/error stderr. Signs, whitespace, non-ASCII digits,
zero, reversed endpoints and extra colons are invalid:

```bash
python -m textstats --lines 0:2 missing.txt
python -m textstats --lines 3:2 missing.txt
python -m textstats --lines=1:2 --lines 2:3 missing.txt
python -m textstats --lines
python -c "from pathlib import Path; Path('bad-range.txt').write_bytes(b'ok\n\xff')"
python -m textstats --lines 1:1 bad-range.txt
```

The first four commands return 2; the last returns 1 for strict decoding, empty
stdout and identifying stderr without a traceback. `--` still permits
range-selected dash-prefixed files, and literal `-` is still a named file.
Omitting `--lines` retains whole-input behavior. Public API functions remain
whole-input with unchanged signatures. Future stdin acquisition is deferred;
the normalized selection semantics do not depend on how complete text is acquired.

## Python API

```python
from textstats import TextStats, count_text, count_file

assert count_text("alpha beta\r\nbeta\rlast two\n") == TextStats(3, 5)
assert count_file("sample.txt") == TextStats(3, 5)
assert count_text("\ufeff") == TextStats(0, 0)
assert count_text("\ufeff", strip_bom=False) == TextStats(1, 1)
```

# TextStats public API and module reference

TextStats exposes exactly `TextStats`, `count_text` and `count_file` directly from the `textstats` package. It requires Python 3.11+ and only the standard library. Importing the package and calling either counting function are silent: no stdout or stderr. The API always counts complete input.

## Signatures and immutable values

```python
from pathlib import Path
from textstats import TextStats, count_text, count_file

assert TextStats(lines=2, words=3) == TextStats(2, 3)
assert count_text("a b\nc") == TextStats(2, 3)
assert count_text("\ufeff", strip_bom=False) == TextStats(1, 1)
assert count_file(Path("sample.txt"), strip_bom=True) == TextStats(3, 5)
```

| Export | Signature / domain | Result and failures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TextStats` | `TextStats(lines: int, words: int)` | Immutable, equal-by-value fields. Nonnegative integers only; bool/non-integers raise TypeError, negative integers raise ValueError. Fields cannot be assigned or deleted. |
| `count_text` | `count_text(text: str, *, strip_bom: bool = True) -> TextStats` | Complete decoded string to immutable statistics, without I/O or shared mutable counting state. |
| `count_file` | `count_file(path: str \| os.PathLike[str], *, strip_bom: bool = True) -> TextStats` | String or string-valued path-like named file to equivalent whole-text counts. OSError subclasses propagate for open/read failures; invalid bytes raise UnicodeDecodeError. |

BOM policy is keyword-only. Behavior outside the stated argument domains is unspecified beyond the explicit statistics constructor validation.

## Counting semantics

Only CRLF, CR and LF terminate logical lines. CRLF is one terminator; each terminator contributes one line, and a final nonempty unterminated segment contributes one. Empty normalized input contributes zero; a trailing terminator creates no phantom line. U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029 remain line content. Word count is `len(text.split())`, using Python Unicode whitespace semantics independently of line terminators.

With the default `strip_bom=True`, remove exactly one leading U+FEFF from the complete input before counting. Preserve a second leading BOM and all interior BOMs. With `False`, retain every BOM as ordinary non-whitespace content. No other normalization occurs.

| Input (escaped) | Default lines / words | Retaining BOM |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Empty | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| `alpha\n` | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 |
| `alpha\r\nbeta\rgamma\n` | 3 / 3 | 3 / 3 |
| `alpha\u2028beta` | 1 / 2 | 1 / 2 |
| `\ufeff` | 0 / 0 | 1 / 1 |
| `\ufeff\ufeff` | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 |

## File acquisition and resource ownership

`count_file` reads complete bytes and decodes strict UTF-8, preserving newline characters. No locale-dependent or fallback decoding and no replacement characters are used. Every file handle opened by the utility closes on success, read failure and decode failure. No partial result is returned after failure. Input bytes remain unchanged. The implementation holds complete decoded input in memory; it makes no bounded-memory promise.

## Module command

Use `python -m textstats [--keep-bom] [--lines START:END] INPUT` from the source root. Exactly one named UTF-8 file is required. Recognized options work before or after INPUT; `--` terminates option parsing for dash-prefixed filenames. Until stdin delivery, literal `-` is a named file. Help (`-h` or `--help`) requires no acquisition.

| Outcome | Status | stdout | stderr |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Count success | 0 | Exactly `lines=<N> words=<N>` plus newline | Empty |
| Help | 0 | Useful usage/options | Empty |
| File open/read or strict decode failure | 1 | Empty | Identifies input and cause, no traceback |
| Missing/extra input, unknown option or invalid/missing/repeated range | 2 | Empty | Useful usage/error, no traceback |

The command validates invocation before opening input and prints counts only after
complete acquisition, strict decode and counting. CLI error translation does not
change the API exception contract. Only exact text output is supported. `--json`, `--json=value` and `--j` fail
with usage status 2 before acquisition; after `--`, a literal `--json` filename
works in whole-input and range modes.

### Range grammar and ordering

One `--lines START:END` or `--lines=START:END` selects inclusive one-based logical
lines. Each endpoint contains only ASCII `0`–`9`, is nonempty and positive, and
START must not exceed END. Leading zeros are decimal. Endpoints have no digit or
value cap and do not change the interpreter's integer conversion guard. Repeated
range options, missing values, signs, whitespace, non-ASCII digits, zero,
reversed endpoints or anything other than one colon are usage errors before
acquisition, even when the file is missing or undecodable.

After complete strict UTF-8 decoding, apply the requested BOM policy exactly
once to the whole input, then number CRLF/CR/LF logical segments and preserve the
available selected segments verbatim. Count the resulting selection without
normalizing again. A selected blank terminated segment is a line with no words;
a final unterminated nonempty segment is a line. A trailing terminator produces
no phantom line. END beyond EOF truncates to available segments; START beyond
EOF or empty normalized input produces zero lines and words. U+0085/U+2028/U+2029
remain line content but may separate words through Unicode whitespace splitting.
An interior BOM exposed at the start of a selected line remains ordinary content.

Named-file bytes are fully acquired and decoded even if END is small: bad UTF-8
after END returns status 1 without partial output. The owned handle closes on
success, read failure and decode failure, and bytes remain unchanged. Selection
makes no bounded-memory promise. Public `count_text` and `count_file` always
count whole input; `--lines` adds no public API argument or export.

Runnable setup, mixed-terminator/blank/interior-BOM/EOF, text, BOM-policy and
invalid/decode examples are in the [README](../README.md). Stdin acquisition is
future work. The normalize/select/count rule is source-independent and can be
reused after complete acquisition without changing public API semantics.

## Module responsibilities

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `textstats.core` | Immutable statistics, once-only BOM normalization, shared CRLF/CR/LF traversal, preserved normalized selection and whole-text counting. |
| `textstats.io` | Strict named-file acquisition and owned-handle lifetime, then shared whole-text counting. |
| `textstats` | Direct public exports; import has no input or process effects. |
| `textstats.cli` | Invocation/range validation before acquisition, BOM/selection ordering, expected failure translation and text rendering. |
| `textstats.__main__` | Minimal module-entry adapter returning the CLI process status. |

Internal helpers are not additional public exports. Range selection reuses preserved logical segments without renormalizing an exposed interior BOM.

"""Owned byte acquisition failures and lifetime are portable controlled seams."""

import io
import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch

from textstats import TextStats, count_file


class FileAcquisitionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_success_closes_owned_binary_handle_and_preserves_terminators(self):
        stream = io.BytesIO(b"a\r\nb\rc\n")
        with patch("textstats.io.open", return_value=stream, create=True) as opener:
            self.assertEqual(count_file("named"), TextStats(3, 3))
        opener.assert_called_once_with("named", "rb")
        self.assertTrue(stream.closed)

    def test_decode_failure_closes_and_returns_no_partial_count(self):
        stream = io.BytesIO(b"valid\n\xff")
        with patch("textstats.io.open", return_value=stream, create=True):
            with self.assertRaises(UnicodeDecodeError):
                count_file("named")
        self.assertTrue(stream.closed)

    def test_read_failure_preserves_exception_and_closes(self):
        class BrokenReader(io.BytesIO):
            def read(self, *args):
                raise OSError("controlled read failure")
        stream = BrokenReader()
        with patch("textstats.io.open", return_value=stream, create=True):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(OSError, "controlled read failure"):
                count_file("named")
        self.assertTrue(stream.closed)

    def test_open_failure_preserves_oserror_subclasses(self):
        for failure in [PermissionError("unreadable"), FileNotFoundError("missing"), IsADirectoryError("directory")]:
            with self.subTest(failure=type(failure)):
                with patch("textstats.io.open", side_effect=failure, create=True):
                    with self.assertRaises(type(failure)) as raised:
                        count_file("named")
                self.assertIs(raised.exception, failure)

# Test-first cycle

Use the cycle for one observable behavior at a time. Read [writing good tests](writing-good-tests.md) before writing or changing a test. Run the project's actual commands; commands in examples are not evidence from the current task.

## RED

1. State the contract and the defect the test should catch. Write a focused test with an independently established expected result.
2. Execute the test before the relevant production change. Inspect the failure and confirm it demonstrates the missing or incorrect behavior.
3. Distinguish a behavioral failure from collection, import, syntax, dependency, or environment failures. Fix test setup or report the blocker before treating the run as RED. An expected exception may be the behavior under test; it is not automatically a setup error.

If the test passes immediately, determine whether it covers existing behavior, misses the intended defect, or exposes a mistaken requirement. Do not alter valid behavior merely to manufacture a failure. Record the actual outcome and resolve the test or contract before proceeding.

## GREEN

Return the failing scenario and observed evidence to the active implementation workflow (**sdd-implement** or **sdd-steer**) for the smallest production change that satisfies the accepted contract. Run the focused test again and the relevant regression checks. If the test still fails, return the failure for repair. Do not weaken a valid assertion to make the implementation pass; correct an erroneous expectation only against independent contract evidence.

Report every observed failure and significant warning. Distinguish new failures, established baseline failures, and environment problems where evidence permits; an unexplained failure remains unresolved. A focused green run does not establish that the whole suite passes.

## REFACTOR and repeat

Improve test clarity and remove test duplication while preserving coverage. Return production-refactoring needs to the active implementation workflow within the accepted task scope. Re-run affected checks after changes; refactoring does not introduce new behavior. Repeat the cycle for remaining scenarios.

Return command and outcome evidence to **sdd-verify** and the active implementation workflow for the required boundary verification, including the declared full suite when project policy or the selected boundary requires it. Do not mark task completion from this development cycle alone.

## Interrupted or non-test-first work

Use existing code and Git evidence without discarding pending work. Characterization tests can establish current behavior; they do not prove a past RED run. When useful and safe, demonstrate regression-test sensitivity against a prior implementation in an isolated worktree or controlled fixture. Label that demonstration accurately and keep the working implementation intact. Report missing evidence, blockers, or an authorized exception rather than claiming strict TDD occurred.

## Record exceptions and gaps

Return the concrete limitation, applicable project policy or existing user authorization, observed alternative checks, and remaining coverage or chronology gap to the active implementation/steering owner and **sdd-report**. Persist those facts with existing task/change evidence; when no location is designated, use the owning entry or its existing linked record, or the ordinary report/commit body for taskless maintenance. Undecided exceptions remain blockers. Missing historical RED, characterization, and isolated sensitivity demonstrations stay accurately labeled; no evidence marker proves unobserved execution order. Do not delete code or fabricate a RED run to reconstruct history.
# Writing good tests

Load this reference whenever writing or changing tests, introducing doubles, or adding test helpers. Each test should protect an observable contract and have a clear explanation of the defect it catches.

## Independent expectations and meaningful failures

- Before writing a test, identify a plausible incorrect branch, argument, result, state transition, or missing effect that it should detect.
- Derive expected values independently: use accepted contracts, literal outcomes, or hand-checked fixtures. Do not call the tested helper to compute both actual and expected values.
- Test outcomes and contract-relevant effects rather than private structure, arbitrary constants, or source-text presence. Exact wording or representation belongs in assertions when the accepted contract requires it.
- Exercise scripts with controlled inputs and inspect outputs, effects, and exit status. Evaluate agent instructions through the consuming agent's behavior; text-presence checks alone cannot demonstrate that a skill works. Structural validators remain useful for format constraints.
- Cover the boundary your code owns. Avoid retesting a dependency's documented internals or trivial forwarding unless your component adds validation, normalization, defaults, lifecycle obligations, or other consequential behavior.

## Real behavior and doubles

Prefer real components and simple controlled fixtures where practical. Use a double when isolation of an external, nondeterministic, costly, or otherwise unsuitable dependency is necessary for the scenario.

| Before introducing a double | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Replacement boundary | Understand the real operation's side effects and preserve those the scenario relies on. Replace the narrow dependency that needs isolation. |
| Returned data | Model realistic contract-compatible structures, including fields relevant to consumers and representative success and failure variants. |
| Assertions | Assert the component's resulting behavior. Argument, order, or call-count checks are appropriate when the interaction itself is part of its contract. |
| Setup complexity | Consider an integration test with real components if the double obscures the behavior or requires extensive imitation of the dependency. |
| Cleanup and helpers | Keep test-only cleanup and helper code in test utilities; do not add production methods solely for tests. Respect actual resource ownership. |

A double's existence or programmed answer is not evidence that the real component works. Ensure that an incorrect production path cannot satisfy the same assertions through a permissive fixture.

## Review sensitivity

Inspect whether plausible faults would fail the tests: for example, a wrong argument, skipped effect, incorrect branch, missing validation, or empty result. If such a fault survives, identify a coverage gap or a test that merely restates the implementation. Use an isolated mutation or controlled faulty fixture when needed to demonstrate sensitivity; do not damage the working code or require mutation tooling by default.

Prefer clear scenario names, narrow assertions, maintainable fixtures, and tests that expose useful failures. Split unrelated behaviors while keeping assertions together when they jointly establish one contract. Re-run changed tests and relevant regressions, and report the evidence and any unresolved gap.

## Examples

These are illustrative Python assertions; replace names and values with the current project's contracts.

```python
# Expected text is independent of the formatter under test.
assert format_record("sample", 3) == "sample:3"

# Reusing the tested formatter on both sides cannot expose its defect.
expected = format_record("sample", 3)
assert format_record("sample", 3) == expected
```

An interaction assertion can be meaningful when the accepted contract specifies it: for example, a component must forward a caller's batch ID unchanged to its sink. Pair that assertion with the relevant real component behavior rather than merely checking that a mock was installed.

# Maintain project documentation

For Markdown output or document work within this skill's scope, apply the shared [Markdown style](../sdd-conventions/references/markdown-style.md): blank lines after headings and around top-level lists and code blocks, plus four-space structural indentation, including nested lists, with exactly one space after each list marker. This applies to direct calls as well as coordinated work; it does not expand editing or review authority.

Choose the requested scope: documentation for affected code, README or selected guides, or a project-wide audit. Read only the relevant references:

| Work | Load |
| --- | --- |
| Module docstrings, API documentation, and explanatory comments | [in-code documentation](references/in-code-documentation.md) |
| README, standalone guides, examples, and navigation | [standalone documentation](references/standalone-documentation.md) |
| Change-scoped or project-wide audit and amendment findings | [review and findings](references/review-and-findings.md) |

Use a current **sdd-orient** handoff for applicable instructions, Git state, target paths, and ownership. **sdd-manage** coordinates the requested editing scope; the active implementation workflow, **sdd-implement** for main task work or **sdd-steer** for a checkpoint amendment, coordinates documentation maintenance after substantive code changes. Read project documentation policies, relevant layout, accepted design, SPEC and PLAN or their active feature equivalents, affected code and tests, and existing documentation as needed. Review can remain read-only; edits require an eligible Git worktree and established ownership of pending changes.

Follow the documentation style specified by governing project documents. Otherwise select an established professional style appropriate to the language and documentation tooling, such as Google-style Python docstrings. Keep documentation accurate, useful, and proportionate to the code's responsibility. Ensure every code module within the selected scope has a professional module docstring or its language's equivalent; a project-wide audit covers every project-owned code module. Report generated or externally maintained modules separately and follow project policy for editing them.

Maintain documentation against both accepted requirements and observed implementation. Clearly distinguish supported behavior from planned capabilities. If a discrepancy requires an amendment to SPEC, PLAN, design, layout, or another authoritative requirement, identify its location, issue, impact, and proposed amendment and report it to the user. Defer the decision to the user; do not amend the governing document or invoke its owning skill automatically. Continue independent documentation work and report anything dependent on that decision as unresolved.

Keep code edits confined to documentation unless additional work is authorized. Do not mark tasks complete, create commits, push, or change hosted objects here; the active implementation workflow owns those operations.

Return the reviewed scope, chosen style and source, documentation changed, checks and observed outcomes, unreviewed or excluded areas, and unresolved findings or user decisions. Use **sdd-report** for a completion summary when requested.
# Completion and status reports

Use the requested boundary from the owning TASKS or FEATURE-TASKS list. A checked box is a claim to compare with actual artifacts, verification output, and Git commits. Inspect the current implementation and relevant acceptance or exit conditions; distinguish task commits, working-branch acceptance, integration into the established target, target publication, and hosted issue state. The target need not be the default branch.

## Task

State task ID, outcome, status, and an implemented-feature summary. Then give the change and reason, files or components affected at a useful level, exact checks and outcomes, commit SHA or pending commit, and resolved issue URL or pending hosted reconciliation if applicable. Describe omissions and unverified conditions plainly. Report **completed** only when task-specific acceptance, documentation and tests, required verification, durable commit, and task-list status are reconciled. An issue closed by the host is not proof.

## Milestone and phase

Summarize the actual capabilities delivered across constituent tasks, rather than a list of checkboxes. Name task IDs and relevant commits, aggregate verification and integration evidence, the PLAN or FEATURE-PLAN exit conditions checked, unresolved defects, and the next stopping boundary. In FEATURE-TASKS, a checked parent covers only that feature's listed work and exits; it does not assert completion of the whole-project parent in TASKS. If some tasks or exits remain, report **partial** or **blocked** with the specific cause.

## Review reports and TODO aggregation

Use the [backend object lifecycle](../../sdd-conventions/references/backend-object-lifecycle.md) for report placement and deferral rules. Main phase reports use `docs/dev/reports/phases/<phase-id>/PHASE-REPORT.md`; milestone reports share that directory as `<milestone-id>.md`. Steering records use its nested `revisions/<revision-id>/`; feature reports remain under their feature directory. Link from the owning review task; draft reports before its commit, without requiring the report to contain its own commit SHA.

For a milestone/phase review report, state stable identity, actual reviewed source, delivered capability, implementation code review coverage and findings, commands/outcomes and limits, repairs/commits, exit assessment, TODO and next boundary. Distinguish inspection from test execution. Include fixed findings and rechecks. An unresolved required check, bug, critical issue or contract violation blocks completion; the report does not waive that blocker. Execution owns report persistence and completion decisions.

Put required repairs and findings of unestablished deferral eligibility in Findings/Blockers, not the deferred TODO. Write `TODO: None` when empty. For each admissible deferred non-critical item include stable finding ID, location/evidence, impact/severity, contract-preserving deferral rationale, proposed solution options/tradeoffs and follow-up owner/scope. Phase reports retain unresolved milestone findings and add phase findings, preserving IDs/provenance. When the full owning task list completes, draft its final IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT.md aggregating unresolved/deferred items and solution options, deduplicated by ID, with references to resolved findings. The final phase review task includes this report; a partial range produces no full-list completion claim. Do not create a second progress journal.

## Interrupted or limited evidence

For an interrupted task or unavailable check, state the last trusted Git state, observed dirty or staged work, checks completed and not completed, and the exact blocker. Do not infer that a half-written commit or test log finished the task. **sdd-orient** identifies interrupted task state, **sdd-manage** coordinates scope, and **sdd-implement** owns continuation; this skill summarizes their evidence. If a performance result is statistically inconclusive, a security fix has only partial regression coverage, or a test run excludes a required suite, make that limit visible in the result.

Use the kind-specific sections in [change kinds](change-kinds.md) where they materially explain the outcome. Keep source attribution near claims: task and document sections for intended behavior; command/output and commits for observed behavior. Do not create a second progress journal or alter TASKS while drafting a report.

## Evidence and test-first limits

Carry task/change identity, tested state, actual commands/outcomes, condition coverage, and material limitations from the verification handoff. Name the designated or owning-entry evidence location; taskless maintenance may use its ordinary report/commit body. Include any authorized test-first exception with its concrete rationale, applicable policy or user authorization, observed alternative evidence, and remaining gaps. Missing RED history remains missing; a sensitivity check or characterization run is not proof of an earlier test-first cycle. Do not add a separate mandatory evidence format.

## Branch boundary

Include the campaign/phase identity and retained directory where applicable. A completed task range in an incomplete main phase is a pushed checkpoint, not a completed integration; report phase work/exits remaining and the paused branch. Report eligible feature archive paths and main task owners, without treating historical lists as executable.

Report working and target branches, starting checkpoint, task or amendment commits, merge SHA and parent tips, working-branch and merged-state verification, and remote containment or pending publication. Distinguish a verified task from a completed integrated workflow. A failed merge or target push remains an explicit blocker even when task commits are verified and pushed. Identify already integrated work without claiming a new merge, and state when an explicit user instruction retained work on its branch.

## Optional capability state

For hosted tracking, report recommendation, pending/confirmed/declined decision, activation and observed provider objects separately. Cite the actual user decision or carried scope. An inactive-state line in an agent-authored plan does not prove refusal; a token or general push authority does not prove activation confirmation. Late reconciliation is current recovery, not proof that projection preceded historical task execution.
# Issue, commit, and PR drafts

Keep the same task identity across all outputs. Use the project-wide ID from its owning TASKS or FEATURE-TASKS entry; include a resolved issue reference only when **sdd-forge** supplies a unique repository and number. Match the requested object's time perspective: an issue describes intended work, while a commit or PR describes actual changes and available evidence.

## Task issue

Return `title` and `body` separately. Format the title as `[<task-id>] <task title>`, using the owning task list. Draft the body from the task outcome, reason and project context, expected scope and dependencies, objective acceptance and prescribed checks, and source document links. Add relevant kind-specific details. For example:

- **Performance:** Describe the problem with the current implementation, explain how the proposed approach may improve it, and identify the measurement plan and any established baseline. Do not present an expected speedup as an achieved result.
- **Security:** State the affected guarantee and risk without exposing exploit instructions or credentials.

**sdd-report** owns the title and body format. Preserve an exact task identity marker when one is supplied. Never invent host labels, milestone associations, issue URLs, or resolution state.

## Git commit

For a first SDD commit or adoption backfill, load **sdd-manage**'s [repository bootstrap](../../sdd-manage/references/repository-bootstrap.md). Confirm the commit owner has included or validly retained root disclosure/usage records and README links within scope. Return missing bootstrap evidence to that owner; drafting does not perform bootstrap or establish a committed result.

Draft a short imperative subject naming the actual change, based on the inspected diff and checks rather than merely the task brief. Use a body when the reason, verification, migration implications or verified issue references need explanation.

### Task commit subjects

For every task-associated commit, use exactly `[<owning-task-id>] <imperative description>`. The single owning task marker must be the first content of the subject, followed by one space and the description. Preserve the exact project-wide ID from TASKS or FEATURE-TASKS. Do not prepend a conventional-commit type/scope, put the ID only at the end, or use multiple task IDs or a task range in the subject. Apply this format to production, tests, documentation and explicit milestone/phase review/report tasks, as well as authorized partial checkpoints and later task-specific repairs or parent-status follow-ups. Describe partial or follow-up work accurately; a subject does not establish completion.

For numeric `T-` IDs padded to at least three digits, `^\[T-[0-9]{3,}\] [^\r\n]+$` checks the basic subject shape. Also check that the ID is the exact owning entry, the subject has no second task identity, and the description is concise, imperative and truthful. A regex alone cannot establish ownership, single-task composition or completion.

| Subject | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| `[T-028] Implement lock delay` | Valid shape for one verified owning task. |
| `[T-030] Complete Milestone 2.4 review` | Valid for the review task's actual result and completion. |
| `[T-028] Record partial lock-delay checkpoint` | Valid shape; retain unchecked status and required checkpoint authority. |
| `feat(mechanics): [T-028] Implement lock delay` | Invalid: content precedes the task marker. |
| `Implement lock delay (T-028)` | Invalid: task marker is not at the beginning. |
| `[T-028, T-029] Implement lock delay and wall kicks` | Invalid: multiple owning tasks. |
| `[T-028] Implement lock delay and close T-029` | Invalid: second task identity, despite passing the shape regex. |

Task closing composition follows **sdd-implement**'s [task commit contract](../../sdd-implement/references/completion-and-checkpoints.md#task-commit-contract): one executable task's result, required evidence and initial completion checkbox together. Return a detected composition conflict to the commit owner; do not merely improve the subject of a bundled or split closing commit.

For preparation, campaign actions or maintenance without an assigned executable task, do not invent a task ID. Merge commits use their integration-summary format and may summarize several completed tasks; they do not close those tasks for the first time.

Use `Refs owner/repo#123` when the commit advances an issue without completing it. Use `Fixes owner/repo#123`, `Resolves owner/repo#123`, or `Closes owner/repo#123` when the commit fully resolves that issue and the evidence supports completion. One task may have multiple verified issue associations, with a separate appropriate reference for each; these references do not permit bundling multiple executable tasks in one closing commit. Omit issue references when no verified association exists. On GitHub, closing keywords may close an issue when the commit reaches the default branch. **sdd-forge** still reconciles issue closure after verified task completion, without waiting for that automation. If verification has not been run, say so in a proposed body rather than claiming it passed. The active implementation workflow makes and checks its commits; **sdd-manage** coordinates persistence for other authorized repository changes.

## Merge commit

Draft a subject identifying the actual feature, revision campaign, steering amendment or selected completed range. For a campaign, include its stable ID and a concise title derived from the final delivered scope, such as `Merge revision 040_a0685b5 — Revision campaign modes`; do not retain a stale opening title when scope changed. A main milestone/task subset does not justify a merge while its phase remains incomplete. Return subject/body separately; the coordinator owns the explicit two-parent integration.

### Campaign integration summary

Every ordinary, nested or reopened revision integration, and every feature, steering, completed phase or accepted document-preparation integration, carries a concise, self-contained summary for [release highlights](../../sdd-forge/references/release-highlights.md#use-integration-summaries-first). Include the following facts, with labels when useful rather than a mandatory machine schema:

- **Objective:** The problem or intended outcome and why it matters.
- **Review:** Actual reviewed scope/coverage and material conclusions; state when no separate review was performed. Do not imply a comprehensive review from a focused amendment.
- **Delivered:** Actual executed scope and consequential features/fixes/documentation or workflow changes, including effects relevant to users. Separate accepted/executed work from proposals, exclusions and unfinished parent work.
- **Verification:** Actual boundary and merged-state checks/results, with relevant counts/environment and evidence limits. Record blocked/unrun checks, material conflict resolutions, compatibility/migration consequences and deferred work when applicable; passing local tests does not prove live acceptance.
- **Integration:** Campaign/phase/preparation identity and mode where applicable, working and return-target branches, full original campaign-opening commit ID, full original branch-off/base commit ID (the starting baseline), and distinct reopening checkpoint when applicable, verified parent/source tips and affected task/action IDs. Apply campaign-opening provenance to campaigns; do not invent a campaign ID/opening for an initial preparation or phase that has none. Git parents establish ancestry; titles/branch names alone do not establish coverage.

A reopened amendment carries forward a concise cumulative summary of the campaign’s retained result and objective/review coverage, then clearly separates the new delta and added actions. Include prior integration, the original campaign-opening commit pointer and original branch-off SHA alongside the reopening checkpoint. Every amendment retains the first opening pointer; do not replace it with an amendment’s first commit. Make the latest cumulative summary sufficient for release highlights without tracing earlier campaign merges: carry forward all relevant retained outcomes, review coverage and material superseded/withdrawn consequences, with original opening provenance and separately identified new delta. Retain relevant earlier information without copying raw prior messages or presenting original delivery as new. Correct superseded outcomes in the cumulative result and distinguish historical checks/source from actual new merged-state verification; inherited verification is not fresh evidence.

Subsequent summaries may also retain compact explicit scope references for the original opening and individual reopenings: identify each opening/reopening commit or checkpoint, added action IDs and its review/execution scope. Carry needed scope distinctions forward in the latest message rather than requiring readers to follow older merge bodies; distinguish these provenance references from the cumulative user outcome and current delta. They are not a new registry or raw chronological transcript.

The campaign-opening commit is the verified first commit opening that campaign and its retained records. It is distinct from the branch-off/shared source checkpoint and from later reopening commits; do not infer it from current branch tips or invent an unavailable identity.

An enclosing integration summarizes the combined delivered result and identifies included nested campaigns/amendments sufficiently to prevent duplicate release highlights. Keep the semantic summary prominent and technical provenance compact; do not substitute raw logs or a list of commit subjects for the outcome.

Phase summaries describe actual completed phase scope, delivery/reviews/exits and verification; retain the full-phase merge gate and report an explicit partial-integration override accurately. Document-preparation summaries identify accepted documents/review coverage and readiness for their dependent stage, without claiming implementation or task completion. Use the plugin’s established `design-docs/*` document-preparation branches; prefixes discover candidates but never establish scope or acceptance. Preserve repeated preparation deltas as distinct scope, with appropriate source/checkpoint evidence.

The message is an **integration summary**, not proof that closure/publication already happened. It is committed before its push and final worktree return; do not claim those future steps succeeded. Closure still requires the applicable verified target publication and return boundary. Review-only publication does not fabricate a closure merge. Do not represent an amendment as completion of the next task, an interrupted parent or a product release. Drafting authorizes no extra work or hosted PR.

```text
Merge revision 040_a0685b5 — Revision campaign modes

Objective: Define nested revisions and eligible campaign amendments.
Review: Assessed campaign routing, branch ownership, closure and reporting.
Delivered: Added both modes, eligibility checks, scoped reopening and
explicit return to the interrupted campaign branch.
Verification: 16 source scenarios checked; 113 support tests passed on the
merged state. Package and link checks passed; live compliance not assessed.
Integration: <campaign/mode, original opening, branch-off/reopening, branches/parents>
```

## Pull request

Draft a title and description only when requested; this skill does not create a PR. Scope the text to the actual branch diff and its included task IDs. Summarize **What**, **Why**, **Verification**, and **Result**; add the relevant fields from [change kinds](change-kinds.md). State the base branch and integration status only when known. List unrun checks, limitations, and remaining work explicitly rather than presenting partial work as complete.

A code health PR should explain the ownership or maintainability problem and the checks supporting behavior preservation. A performance PR should include baseline and current times, input size, environment, method, and whether the measured gain is meaningful. Do not imply that GitHub PR operations are available through **sdd-forge**.
